title: VPC Peering Matrix + Cluster Health Canvas: Unified Private Console Surface
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Admins managing Private/VPC deployments currently jump between multiple pages to understand networking relationships, cluster health, and upgrade status. Goal: design a single, scannable console surface that combines an interactive VPC peering matrix with a cluster-level health canvas and upgrade timeline while surfacing cost signals and quick mitigation actions. Audience: platform engineers, SREs, and customer success during onboarding/troubleshooting. Proposed components: 1) Peering matrix (interactive adjacency matrix) showing peering status, traffic patterns, and applied policies; 2) Cluster Health Canvas (cards for each cluster showing SLOs, recent incidents, drift warnings, node utilization, and KV cache hit rate); 3) Upgrade orchestration row (timeline with canary segments, estimated risk, and cost delta); 4) Cost + latency mini-panel summarizing incremental cost per routing decision; 5) Action bar for quick operations (retrigger upgrade, open support runbook, create peering ticket). Accessibility and compactness prioritized for 4-6 clusters on screen. This ticket covers high-fidelity prototype, interaction spec, engineering handoff, and visual QA acceptance.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive peering matrix prototype in Figma that allows filtering by region, status, and policy and shows hover details (latency, throughput, last sync)
Cluster Health Canvas cards present SLO badge, last 24h errors, node CPU/memory sparkline, KV cache hit-rate, and a clear link to cluster logs
Upgrade timeline shows active rollout segments, estimated % completion, rollback control, and an inline cost delta estimate
Design tokens and components use Redwood Console system fonts/colors; spacing and responsive behavior documented for 1280px and 1440px breakpoints
Design handoff includes a clickable prototype, a redlines page, and a short engineering acceptance checklist in Confluence
comments: 2025-03-12 Maya Chen: Kickoff — consolidated brief from PM (PM-417) and ENG reliability asks. Primary constraints: private deployments cannot send telemetry outside VPC; latency numbers must be calculated from internal metrics. Planning to sketch peering adjacency first.

2025-03-14 Oliver Ruiz: Early wireframes uploaded to figma. Two layout variants: matrix-left/canvas-right and stacked canvas with modal matrix. Engineering prefers matrix-left for faster glanceability. Linked: Figma v1.

2025-03-15 Ana Patel (PM): Reviewed and suggested adding cost delta micro-metric near upgrade actions. Also requested keyboard shortcuts for common actions (retrigger, mark investigated). Marked as high-impact for enterprise customers.

2025-03-16 Priya Nair (Eng): Feasibility review: adjacency matrix must load lazily and support server-side pagination for >50 VPCs. Suggested adding offline state for clusters with no metrics and using an API flag for sensitive fields in private mode. Raised dependency ENG-2209 for backend endpoints.

2025-03-17 Security (Liam O'Connor): Noted that peering hover should not expose raw IPs unless user has permission. Security review required for exposing LLN and KV cache metrics. Added label 'security-sensitive'.

2025-03-18 Maya Chen: Usability test with two internal SREs. Feedback: prefer a compact 'critical-first' toggle that collapses non-critical clusters. Also asked for one-click 'open runbook' from cluster card. Updated prototype with critical-first toggle and runbook link.

2025-03-18 Oliver Ruiz: Preparing engineering handoff. Created Confluence handoff doc and included component props table. Added ENG checklist: API contracts (ENG-2209), telemetry toggle (ENG-2231), and RBAC check (SEC-131).
